title: Pancyclic Excess Edges
description: Let h(n) be the minimum excess edges beyond n for an n-vertex pancyclic graph (containing all cycle lengths 3 to n). Estimate h(n): is h(n) >= log_2 n + log* n - O(1)? Known: log_2(n-1) - 1 <= h(n) <= log_2 n + log* n + O(1).

overview.historicalContext: The study of pancyclic graphs originated with Bondy (1971), who proved his celebrated metaconjecture: any condition implying Hamiltonicity (except bipartiteness) also implies pancyclicity. He conjectured bounds on h(n), the minimum excess edges for pancyclicity, but without published proofs. The lower bound h(n) >= floor(log_2(n-1)) - 1 was finally proved by Griffin in 2013, over 40 years after Bondy's conjecture. George, Khodkar, and Wallis (2016) proved the upper bound h(n) <= floor(log_2 n) + log* n + O(1) via explicit hierarchical constructions using Hamiltonian cycles with carefully placed chords. The appearance of the iterated logarithm log* n is remarkable -- it is one of the few natural combinatorial problems where log* appears in the answer. Erdos believed the upper bound is tight but could not even prove h(n) - log_2 n -> infinity, leaving a gap of only log* n + O(1) between upper and lower bounds. This makes Problem #1016 one of the most precisely understood yet still open problems in extremal graph theory.
overview.problemStatement: Estimate $h(n)$, the minimum excess edges for pancyclic $n$-vertex graphs. Is $h(n) \geq \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + \log^* n - O(1)$?
overview.proofStrategy: We formalize pancyclic graphs as those containing cycles of all lengths 3 through n, define the excess function h(n) as a supremum, and give a recursive definition of the iterated logarithm. The main conjecture (matching the upper bound), the weaker open question (h(n) - log_2 n -> infinity), Bondy's lower bound (Griffin 2013), the George-Khodkar-Wallis upper bound (2016), structural properties (Hamiltonian baseline, Bondy's quadratic threshold, monotonicity), and small cases are all stated as axioms.
keyInsights: A pancyclic graph contains cycles of all lengths 3 through n, which is much stronger than Hamiltonicity (just length n) -- the extra edges pay for the shorter cycles
Bondy's lower bound log_2(n-1) - 1 arises because each chord added to a Hamiltonian cycle can roughly double the set of achievable cycle lengths, requiring at least log_2(n) chords
The George-Khodkar-Wallis upper bound log_2 n + log* n + O(1) uses a hierarchical chord structure where each level of the hierarchy adds one chord and covers a tower of cycle lengths
The iterated logarithm log* n appears naturally because the construction proceeds in tower-like levels: each level covers cycle lengths from 2^{2^{...}} down to 3
Even proving h(n) - log_2 n -> infinity is open, showing how difficult it is to improve the logarithmic lower bound by even an unbounded additive term
The gap log* n + O(1) between bounds is so slowly growing that it equals 5 for all practically realizable values of n, yet closing it remains elusive

sections.title: Header and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring with problem statement, key results, and references to Bondy (1971), Griffin (2013), George-Khodkar-Wallis (2016), and OEIS A105206. Imports Mathlib for SimpleGraph, Nat.Log, reals, and tactics.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines IsPancyclic (contains all cycle lengths 3 to n), pancyclicExcess h(n) as the min excess edges, and iteratedLog (log* n) via recursion on Nat.log 2.

sections.title: Main Conjecture and Weaker Question
sections.summary: Two open problems: (1) h(n) >= log_2 n + log* n - O(1) (matching the GKW upper bound), and (2) the weaker h(n) - log_2 n -> infinity that Erdos could not prove.

sections.title: Known Bounds
sections.summary: Bondy's lower bound floor(log_2(n-1)) - 1 (Griffin 2013 proof) and the George-Khodkar-Wallis upper bound floor(log_2 n) + log* n + O(1) from 2016.

sections.title: Structural Properties and Small Cases
sections.summary: Hamiltonian baseline (h(n) >= 0), Bondy's quadratic threshold (n^2/4 edges suffice but is far from tight), monotonicity of pancyclicity, exact values h(3) = 0 and h(4) = 1, and the tightness of the bounds gap.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures Erdos Problem #1016 on the minimum excess edges for pancyclic graphs. The bounds log_2(n-1) - 1 <= h(n) <= log_2 n + log* n + O(1) leave a gap of only log* n + O(1), making this one of the most precisely bounded yet open extremal problems. The appearance of the iterated logarithm is a remarkable feature of this problem.
conclusion.implications: Resolving the precise value of h(n) would determine the exact edge threshold for pancyclicity and would likely require new techniques for analyzing cycle lengths in sparse graphs. The result could connect to the broader theory of graph properties at the Hamiltonian threshold.
openQuestions: Is h(n) >= log_2 n + log* n - O(1), matching the George-Khodkar-Wallis upper bound?
Does h(n) - log_2 n -> infinity? (Erdos could not prove even this weaker claim)
What are the exact values of h(n) for small n beyond h(3) = 0 and h(4) = 1?
Is there a natural combinatorial interpretation of why log* n appears in the answer?
Does the analogous problem for vertex-pancyclic graphs (every vertex on cycles of all lengths) have a similar answer?
